transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Good morning. Please take a seat. What brings you in today?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: I have been having really bad adage for about 4 days now.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Can you describe the pain for me?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: It's mostly on the right side, behind my eye. It drops bright light makes it much worse.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Have you felt sick at all or been vomiting? I

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: know she has yesterday morning, but I have actually been sick.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Any changes to your vision, blurring or flashing lights?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Sometimes there are little zigzag lines before it starts.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Have you had headaches like this before?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Not sure this bad. I get normal headaches, but nothing like this.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Are you taking any medications at the moment?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Just pelsomol when it gets bad. It does not help much.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Let me check your blood pressure. Your blood pressure is 140 over 90, which is elevated. Pupils are equal and reactive. No next -tiffness. This looks like migraine with aura and your blood pressure is higher than what I would like. I am going to prescribe some atriptin 50mg for the attacks. Keep a headache diary for 2 weeks. Come back in 2 weeks so we can recheck your blood pressure. If the pain becomes suddenly severe or your develop weakness or confusion, go to the emergency department immediately.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Understood. Thank you doctor.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Hello, come in. What happened?

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: I twisted my ankle playing football yesterday evening.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Which ankle?

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: The right one. Could you walk

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: on it afterwards?

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Barely I limped off the pitch and it's been swollen since. Did you hear a pop or a crack at the time? No, nothing like that. Have you put anything on it? Just ice last night and I kept it up on a cushion. Any previous injuries to that ankle? I sprained it about two years ago, the same side.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Let me have a look. There is swelling over the lateral malacious and tenderness on the outer side. No bony tenderness at the posterior edge. You can bear weight just about. Range of motion is reduced by pain. This is a lateral ankle sprain, grade 2. I do not think it is fractured and by the outower rules you do not need an x -ray. Rest, ice compression and elevation for the next three days. Take eye -proofing for 400 mg, 3 times daily with food. Start gentle movement after day 3. If you still cannot bear weight in a week, come back and we will arrange imaging.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: How long until I can play again?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Realistically 4 to 6 weeks and only after you can hop on it without pain.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Hi there, what can I do for you?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: My throat has been really sore since Saturday and it hurts to swallow. Do you have a fever? I felt hot last night. I didn't take my temperature.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay, any cough?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: No cough at all actually.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Any swelling in your neck or tenderness?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Yeah, under my jaw feels tender.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Anyone at home or at work? Unwell?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: My daughter had a sore throat last week.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Let me examine you. Temperature is 38 .2. The tonsils are enlarged with white exudite on both sides. There is tender cervical lymphodenum pethi, no cough reported. That gives you a center score of 4, which makes bacterial infection likely rather than viral. Right. I will start you on phenoxymythylene penicillin 250mg, 4 times a day for 10 days. Finish the whole course even when you feel better, take parasitomol for the pain and drink plenty of fluids.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Yeah, okay.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: If you develop difficulty breathing or you cannot swallow your own saliva, that is an emergency and you should be seen straight away.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Good afternoon. This is your 3 month diabetes review, isn't it?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: That's right. It's been about 3 months since the last one.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: How have things been going?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Honestly mixed. I have been taking the net form, net for mind every day, but my sugar are still higher than I had like in the morning. I have been checking most days, usually around 8 or 9 before breakfast. In the evening, it's better. Maybe 6 or 7. I have been trying to walk more, about 20 minutes most days. But work has been busy and I have missed some days. My weight is about the same at last time.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Any high pose? Any episodes of feeling shaky, sweaty, confused?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: No. Nothing like that.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: How about your feet? Any numbness or tingling?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: A bit of tingling in my toes, it's night sometimes.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Okay. Any changes to your vision?

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Not that I have noticed.

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Let me examine you and go through your results. Your blood pressure today is 132 over 84. Weight is unchanged at 86 kilograms. Your HP A1C has come back at 58 millimetres per month. The Tingling is not showing up as a myelible nerve damage yet. Overall, this is type 2 diabetes with some optimal glycemic control and some early neuropathic symptoms that are not yet confirmed on examination. I am going to increase your metformin to 1 gram twice daily. Please continue monitoring your morning readings and bring the record next time. I will refer you for retinal pain. I will use retinal screening which is due and I would like to repeat bloods in 3 months. If the tingling in your feet gets worse or spread, let me know sooner rather than waiting.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Should I change anything about my diet?

transcript.speaker: DOCTOR
transcript.text: Focus on the morning's reading. First, I will book you in with the diabetes nurse to go through evening meals. Since that is what usually drives the fasting numbers.

transcript.speaker: PATIENT
transcript.text: Alright. Thank you doctor.
